From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Draft: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) GA customer comms — review by Fri 2/13

Team —

We’re targeting GA for Dedicated autoscaling bounds (customer-configured min/max capacity) and the customer-facing comms need a final pass this week.

Ask: Please review the draft by EOD Fri 2/13. Priya — would love exec sign-off on the positioning + the “hard max” language.

Google Doc: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds - GA Customer Comms Draft v3 (link)
Attachment: Console screenshot - Scaling History (PNG)

Key things we must get right:
- Clear explanation of what’s changing (strict max cap; min floor; improved scale decisions).
- Defaults/backfill for existing Dedicated pools.
- How to avoid throttling (max too low) + what customers will see in Console.
- “What happens during maintenance/drains” language (no surprises).

Draft email copy (below) for quick inline comments:

---
Subject: New Dedicated autoscaling controls: set minimum + maximum capacity (GA)

Hi <FirstName>,

We’re excited to share that Dedicated autoscaling bounds are now generally available.

What’s new
You can now configure a minimum and maximum capacity for each Dedicated pool:
- Minimum capacity (min): a floor that helps maintain predictable latency by keeping a baseline of GPUs online.
- Maximum capacity (max): a strict cap to help keep spend predictable during bursts or anomalous traffic.

Why this matters
Previously, autoscaling was primarily reactive and some customers saw unexpected scale-ups (spend) or aggressive scale-downs (performance risk). Bounds provide explicit guardrails while still allowing the autoscaler to respond to real demand.

Defaults for existing pools
For existing Dedicated pools, we’ll apply conservative default bounds based on your current steady-state capacity and hardware class.
- If you’d prefer to set these explicitly before the defaults take effect, reply to this email or contact your TAM/CS and we can coordinate timing.

How to choose min/max (avoiding throttling)
Setting max too low can result in throttling and increased latency during peaks.
General guidance:
- Set min to cover your typical baseline load (weekday average).
- Set max to cover your expected peak load (p95/p99) plus a safety margin.
- If your traffic has predictable spikes (e.g., top-of-hour, batch jobs), consider temporarily raising max ahead of that window.

Visibility + audit trail
In the Redwood Console, you can view Scaling History for your pool, including:
- scale-up/scale-down events
- when a scale decision was clamped to your max
- basic “why did we scale?” context (e.g., queue depth / utilization)

Notes / behavior details
- Max is enforced as a hard cap for autoscaling.
- If the fleet cannot meet a requested min due to capacity constraints or maintenance, we will make best effort and surface the condition in Console.

If you’d like help sizing your bounds, share a traffic profile (QPS/token rate and peak windows) and we’ll recommend an initial configuration.

Thanks,
Lauren
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
---

Open questions I’d like reviewers to weigh in on:
1) Do we want to explicitly mention predictive scaling in GA comms, or keep it as “improved scale decisions” until confidence scoring has more mileage?
2) “Best effort min” phrasing — ok for GA, or too hand-wavy?

Thanks,
Lauren


From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) GA customer comms — review by Fri 2/13

Edits inline in the doc, but headline feedback here:

- I’d name the customer problem more directly ("prevent surprise spend" + "avoid latency during scale-down") and call out that max is a strict cap. That’s the core value prop.
- I would NOT mention “predictive” in the outward email for GA. It reads like a promise we’ll be held to (and Support will get the “why didn’t you pre-scale?” questions).
- Suggest we add a single sentence about what customers can do if max leads to throttling: “raise max or contact us for Dedicated capacity planning.”

Also, can we avoid the phrase “anomalous traffic” (sounds like we’re blaming them)? Maybe “unexpected spikes”.

Soojin
Product Marketing


From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:28 AM PT
Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) GA customer comms — review by Fri 2/13

+1 to keeping predictive out of the GA blast.

Two CS notes based on recent tickets:
- SUP-4874: customer set max too low, then saw throttling and assumed Redwood “broke autoscaling.” We need an explicit warning: “max is a budget guardrail; if hit, requests may queue/throttle.”
- SUP-4821: customer expectation is that max is strict and auditable. We should emphasize “max is enforced” + “Scaling History shows clamp events.”

Also, can we add a short “recommended starting point” for current customers (e.g., “we’ll set max to X% above current peak unless you override”)? It reduces anxiety about defaults.

Rachel
Customer Success

Adding Support perspective:

- Please include one line on how to interpret “clamped to max” in Console so customers don’t treat it as an error (“system respected your configured max”).
- If we’re mentioning “best effort min,” we need to be precise that maintenance/drain may temporarily go below min and this will be visible as a status/notice.

We’re drafting macros + escalation checklist under INT-1338; once you finalize wording, we’ll align the macros with the customer language.

Dev

Left comments in the doc re: terminology consistency.

Request: can we standardize on “min_gpus / max_gpus” in the comms? Some customers think “replicas” = pods, not GPUs. If the Console uses “GPUs,” then the email should too.

Also suggest adding a short snippet that points to the docs page (“Learn more: Configuring Dedicated autoscaling bounds”) so this doesn’t become a long email.

Elliot
Docs

Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) GA customer comms — review by Fri 2/13

Reviewed.

I’m OK with “max is enforced as a hard cap for autoscaling.” Keep it plain.

On “best effort min”: please tighten. Something like:
- “We will maintain at least min_gpus under normal operating conditions. During maintenance or regional capacity constraints, temporary dips below min_gpus can occur; we surface this in Console and will return to min_gpus as capacity becomes available.”

Agree with Soojin/Rachel: do not mention predictive for GA. Keep the customer promise limited to what we can stand behind 100%.

Once edits are in, I can sign off.

Priya

Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) GA customer comms — review by Fri 2/13

Made updates in the doc based on everyone’s feedback:

- Removed “predictive” mention entirely.
- Standardized terminology to min_gpus/max_gpus (and “GPUs” in explanations).
- Added explicit warning + mitigation language for hitting max (queueing/throttling; raise max / contact CS for sizing).
- Tightened min behavior per Priya’s wording.
- Added a short “what to expect for defaults” paragraph: we’ll set initial max to current observed peak + buffer (exact % in CS internal notes), and we’ll notify customers in advance.
- Added one sentence on interpreting “clamped to max” (“respected your configured max”) to reduce confusion.

Priya — when you have a moment, please re-check the updated draft and reply with approval so we can hand off to CS/Support and schedule send.

Lauren
